title: Miss Minute To The End — Scripting Guide
description: Complete reference documentation for the Miss Minutes animation scripting language, covering commands, variables, loops, expressions, audio sync, and best practices.
content: TVA SCRIPTING GUIDE ⚡ Launch Studio Miss Minutes Scripting Language A complete guide to the Miss Minutes Studio v2 scripting language — featuring variables, loops, if/else, sequences, audio control, and more. Table of Contents Quick Start Timing Syntax Variables & Expressions Control Flow — if / elif / else Loops — repeat & while Sequences (Reusable Blocks) Together (Parallel Execution) Wait Break, Continue & End All Commands Reference Audio Commands Expressions List Moves List Effects (fx) List Full Script Examples Understanding Errors 1 · Quick Start Open the studio, clear the editor, and paste this — then press ⚡ Play : # My first animation 0 background tva 1 enter left 2 expression happy 2 say "Hello! I'm Miss Minutes!" for 3 6 move wave 8 exit right Tip Each line that starts with a number is a timed event — the number is the time in seconds when that command runs. Keyboard shortcuts Ctrl+Enter — Start playback with countdown Escape — Stop playback immediately Tab — Indent selected lines (2 spaces) Shift+Tab — Un-indent selected lines { + Enter — Auto-closes the block with } 2 · Timing Syntax Every top-level event needs a time before the command. Time is always in seconds . Syntax Meaning Example N Absolute time (seconds) 5 → at exactly 5 s N.N Fractional seconds 2.5 → at 2.5 s M:SS Minutes:Seconds 1:30 → at 90 s +N Relative — N seconds after previous line's time +2 → 2 s later +N.N Relative fractional +0.5 → 0.5 s later 0 background tva 2.5 enter left 1:00 say "One minute in!" for 3 +5 expression excited # 5 s after previous = 1:05 +2 exit right # 5+2 = 1:07 Block syntax (multiple commands at one time) Use at TIME { … } or TIME { … } to run several commands at the same moment: at 5 { expression excited move bounce say "Three things at 5s!" for 2 } Order within a block Commands inside { } run sequentially by default (each waits for the previous to finish). Use together { } to run them in parallel. 3 · Variables & Expressions Variables let you store values and use them anywhere in the script. Declaring variables var count = 5 var name = "Miss Minutes" var fast = true Where to declare var at the top level (before any timed event) is a global variable. var inside a block only lasts for that block. Reading a variable Prefix the name with $ : say $name for 3 repeat $count { fx sparkle 4 wait 0.5 } Updating a variable — set set count = $count + 1 set name = "Hello " + $name Operators Operator Meaning Example + Add / concatenate strings $x + 2 · "Hi " + $name - Subtract $x - 1 * Multiply $x * 3 / Divide $x / 2 % Modulo (remainder) $x % 3 == Equal $x == 5 != Not equal $x != 0 < > <= >= Comparisons $x > 3 && Logical AND $x > 0 && $x < 10 || Logical OR $x == 0 || $x == 5 ! Logical NOT !$active ( ) Grouping ($x + 2) * 3 Variable interpolation in strings var n = 7 say "I found $n variants!" for 3 4 · Control Flow — if / elif / else if $count > 5 { expression excited say "Lots of them!" for 2 } elif $count == 5 { expression neutral say "Just five" for 2 } else { expression sad say "Not many..." for 2 } You can have as many elif branches as you like. else is optional. Conditions support any boolean expression (see operators above). Tip Use not as an alternative to ! : if not $done { … } 5 · Loops — repeat & while repeat N { … } Runs the block exactly N times. N can be a variable. repeat 4 { fx sparkle 3 wait 0.6 } # Use $__i for the current iteration index (0-based) repeat 5 { say "Loop $__i " for 1 } while CONDITION { … } Keeps looping until the condition becomes false. Always make sure the condition will eventually be false, or use break . var i = 0 while $i < 5 { expression excited set i = $i + 1 wait 0.8 } Safety limit The engine stops any while loop after 10 000 iterations automatically to prevent freezing. 6 · Sequences (Reusable Blocks) A sequence is a named block you can call from anywhere — like a function. sequence greet { expression happy move wave say "Hi there!" for 2 fx sparkle 4 } # Now call it at any time: at 2 { call greet } at 8 { call greet } at 14 { call greet } Declare sequences before any timed events (at the top of the script). Sequences can call other sequences. Sequences can use global variables. 7 · Together (Parallel Execution) By default commands in a block run one after another. together { } makes them all start at the same time: together { move dance say "Watch me dance!" for 3 fx sparkle 8 } Tip Use together for things that should happen simultaneously — like playing music while talking, or doing an effect while moving. 8 · Wait Pauses execution of the current block for N seconds. Essential inside loops and sequences: repeat 5 { expression happy wait 0.5 expression surprised wait 0.5 } wait 2 # wait 2 seconds wait 0.25 # wait 250ms wait $dur # wait from a variable 9 · Break, Continue & End Keyword Effect break Exit the current loop immediately continue Skip the rest of this iteration and go to the next end Stop the entire animation immediately # Play sparkles but stop at 3 var n = 0 repeat 100 { fx sparkle 3 set n = $n + 1 wait 0.5 if $n == 3 { break } } # Skip even iterations repeat 6 { if $__i % 2 == 0 { continue } fx heart 3 wait 0.5 } 10 · All Commands Reference The for N option on most commands means "do this and automatically undo it N seconds later". Command Description Options expression NAME Set a facial expression. Use for N to return to neutral after N seconds. for N move NAME Perform a body movement animation. for N look DIRECTION Point eyes in a direction. Use for N to return to center. for N say "TEXT" Show caption + lip-sync. Duration auto-calculated from text length. for N talk Lip-sync without caption text. for N fx NAME [count] Particle effect. Optional count (default 5). — enter SIDE Character slides in from left or right. — exit SIDE Character slides out. Use for N for duration. for N peek SIDE Character peeks in and then retreats. for N walk DELTA Move character by DELTA (−1 to +1) over time. for N walkTo X Move character to absolute X position (−1 to +1). for N blink Force one blink cycle. — lean DEGREES Tilt body. Use for N to return to upright. for N find "QUERY" TVA timeline finder animation. for N background NAME Change background scene. Use for N to revert. for N background video "file" Play a video as background. from N to N loop rate N sound for N wait N Pause block execution for N seconds. — Directions for look left · right · up · down · center · upleft · upright · downleft · downright · farleft · farright · offleft · offright 11 · Audio Commands Audio files must be uploaded via the Media panel first (drag & drop or use the upload button). Command Description audio "file.mp3" Load and play an audio file audio "file.mp3" vol 0.8 Set volume (0.0 to 1.0) when starting audio "file.mp3" from 30 Start playback at 30 seconds into the file audio "file.mp3" for 10 Play for 10 seconds, then pause audio.pause Pause playback audio.resume Resume after pause audio.stop Stop and reset to beginning stopaudio Alias for audio.stop audio.volume 0.5 Set volume immediately (0.0 – 1.0) audio.seek 30 Jump to 30 seconds in the file audio.rate 1.5 Set playback speed (0.1 – 4.0, default 1.0) audio.loop Enable looping audio.fade 0 2 Fade volume to 0 over 2 seconds # Full audio example at 0 { audio "background.mp3" vol 0.6 } at 30 { audio.fade 0 3 # fade out over 3 seconds wait 3 audio.stop } 12 · Expressions List Use with: expression NAME or expression NAME for N neutral # Default resting face happy sad angry surprised confused excited serious mischievous curious shy proud worried sleepy determined smug horrified apologetic loving thinking disappointed 13 · Moves List Use with: move NAME bounce wave dance spin shake nod bow jump stomp wiggle float pulse wag shiver strut snap curtsy salute flip slide 14 · Effects (fx) List Use with: fx NAME or fx NAME COUNT sparkle heart star confetti explosion snow rain fire lightning bubble music clock question exclaim arrow diamond flower leaf skull trophy 15 · Full Script Examples Example 1: Simple greeting 0 background tva 1 enter left 2 expression happy 2 say "Hello! Great to see you!" for 3 6 move wave 8 exit right Example 2: Countdown with loop var count = 5 at 2 { expression excited while $count > 0 { say $count for 0.8 fx sparkle 3 set count = $count - 1 wait 0.9 } say "Blast off!" for 2 fx explosion 10 } Example 3: Mood switcher with sequences var mood = "happy" var rounds = 3 sequence showMood { if $mood == "happy" { expression happy fx heart 5 } elif $mood == "excited" { expression excited fx sparkle 8 } else { expression neutral } say "Feeling $mood !" for 2 wait 2.5 } 0 enter left at 1 { repeat $rounds { call showMood if $mood == "happy" { set mood = "excited" } elif $mood == "excited" { set mood = "happy" } } move bow } Example 4: Audio + animation sync at 0 { background nexus audio "intro.mp3" vol 0.7 enter left } at 2 { together { expression excited move dance say "Welcome to the TVA!" for 4 } } at 10 { audio.fade 0 3 wait 3 audio.stop exit right } 16 · Understanding Errors Errors appear in the Problems panel below the editor. Click any error to jump to that line. Error message What it means Fix Lines must start with a time… A top-level line doesn't begin with a number Add a time: 5 expression happy Expected variable name after "var" You wrote var = 5 without a name var x = 5 Missing closing "}" You opened a block { but never closed it Add } at the end of the block Expected "{" An if / while / repeat has no block Add { after the condition Unknown command "xyz" The command name is misspelled or unsupported Check the commands table above Expected sequence name after "call" call without a name call mySeq Live feedback The editor shows errors as you type — red gutter marks on error lines, yellow for warnings. No need to run the animation to find mistakes. 👨‍💻 Created By Prashant Pandey Web developer & creator of Miss Minute To The End — a TVA animation studio inspired by Loki Season 1. 🌐 prashant-pandey.com.np 📂 More Projects ← Project Home ⚡ Launch Studio ↑ Back to Top TVA Miss Minute To The End · Guide v2 · by Prashant Pandey

title: Miss Minute To The End
description: An open-source, browser-based TVA animation studio inspired by Loki Season 1. Script Miss Minutes animations with variables, loops, audio sync, and real-time preview.
content: Skip to main content TVA Miss Minute To The End About Features Scripting Developer Guide ⚡ Launch Studio Open Source · Browser-Based · No Install Miss Minute To The End "The beginning is the ending." A TVA-inspired browser animation studio — script Miss Minutes to life with a modern programming language. Loops, variables, audio, real-time preview. All in your browser. ⚡ Launch Studio 📖 Scripting Guide animation.mmscript # Miss Minute To The End — sample script var greeting = "Hello from the TVA!" var loops = 3 sequence intro { expression excited say $greeting for 3 fx sparkle 6 } 0 background timeline 0.5 enter left at 2 { call intro } at 6 { repeat $loops { move dance wait 0.8 } expression happy } +5 exit right 🔁 Loops & While 📦 Variables 🔀 If / Elif / Else 🎯 Sequences 🎵 Audio Sync ⚡ Live Preview 📱 Mobile Ready 🔓 Open Source The Story Inspired by the Sacred Timeline Miss Minute To The End is a passion project born from love for the TVA universe in Loki Season 1 . The character Miss Minutes — the cheerful clockwork mascot of the Time Variance Authority — captured imaginations worldwide. This project brings her to life in your browser. The title "The Beginning Is the Ending" reflects both the circular nature of the TVA's Sacred Timeline and the creative philosophy behind this tool: every animation you script begins and ends in a loop of infinite creative possibility. What started as an experiment with SVG procedural animation grew into a fully-featured studio with its own scripting language — because when you love a character enough, you build a whole programming environment to animate her. The beginning is the ending. And the ending? Well, sugar, that's just another beginning. — Miss Minutes, TVA · Inspiration for this project 🕐 MISS MINUTES The clockwork mascot of the Time Variance Authority. Cheerful · Knowledgeable · A little bit ominous. Procedurally animated in SVG — every expression, blink, and lip-sync driven entirely by a scripting language you write yourself. What's Inside Studio Features Everything you need to direct, script, and preview TVA-style animations — all running locally in your browser. 🖊️ Modern Scripting Language Write animations in a clean, readable language with variables, if/else, loops, sequences, and parallel execution — like a real programming language. ✨ Live Syntax Highlighting The built-in code editor highlights every token in real time — keywords, commands, variables, strings, numbers — with error markers in the gutter. 🎭 20+ Expressions Happy, sad, mischievous, excited, confused, scared, smug, loving — all driven by a procedural SVG rig with smooth interpolated transitions. 💃 Moves & Animations Bounce, dance, spin, wave, bow, flip, slide, strut — character body animations that respond to timing and loop control from your script. 🎵 Full Audio Control Load audio files, control volume, seek, pause, resume, fade in/out, set playback rate, and loop — all with simple one-line commands. ⚡ Particle Effects Sparkle, heart, star, confetti, explosion, fire, lightning, music notes, clock icons — trigger any effect with a single fx command. 🖥️ Live Stage Preview Watch your animation play in real-time on the stage panel. Switch between 16:9 and 9:16 aspect ratios. Press Play for a full-screen countdown performance. 🐛 Smart Error Detection The Problems panel shows exactly which line has an error and why — with helpful hints on how to fix it. Click any error to jump directly to that line. 📱 Mobile Optimised A separate mobile stylesheet provides a touch-friendly single-column layout with larger tap targets, optimised font sizes, and landscape support. Scripting Language Write animations like code The Miss Minutes scripting language is designed to be easy to learn but powerful enough for complex productions. Here's a taste of what you can write: Variables + If Loops Sequences Audio # ── Variables & conditional logic ───────────────────── var score = 8 var name = "Miss Minutes" at 2 { if $score > 7 { expression excited say " $name approves! Score: $score " for 3 fx sparkle 8 } elif $score > 4 { expression neutral say "Could be better…" for 2 } else { expression sad say "Oh dear, sugar…" for 2 } } All supported commands expression Set facial expression + optional auto-revert move Body animation (bounce, dance, wave…) look Point eyes in any direction say "text" Caption + automatic lip-sync talk Lip-sync without caption text fx Particle effect with count control enter / exit Character stage entries and exits peek Peek in from side and retreat walk / walkTo Move character across stage background Animated scene backgrounds + video audio Load and play audio files audio.fade Smooth volume fade over duration blink Force a manual blink cycle lean Tilt character body at angle find TVA timeline search animation wait Pause block execution N seconds if / elif / else Conditional branching logic repeat / while Loop structures with counter sequence / call Reusable named blocks together Run commands in parallel break / continue Loop control flow end Stop the entire animation Workflow How It Works From first line of script to full-screen performance in four steps. 01 Write Your Script Use the built-in editor with live syntax highlighting, auto-indent, error detection, and a command palette. No external tools needed. 02 Upload Media Drag and drop audio or video files into the Media Library. They're instantly accessible in your script by filename. 03 Preview Live Click Preview to watch your animation on the stage in real-time. Fix errors in the Problems panel and iterate instantly. 04 Play Full-Screen Press Play for a cinematic 5-4-3-2-1 countdown and full-screen performance. Escape to stop at any time. Created By 👨‍💻 Developer & Creator Prashant Pandey A passionate web developer with a love for creative, interactive experiences. Miss Minute To The End was built entirely in vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript — no frameworks, no build tools — as a showcase of what modern browsers can do. From procedural SVG character rigs to a custom scripting language interpreter, every line was crafted by hand with care for both code quality and user experience. 🌐 prashant-pandey.com.np 📂 More Projects Ready to Begin? Start animating Miss Minutes No installation. No account. Just open the studio and start writing. ⚡ Launch Studio 📖 Read the Guide TVA Miss Minute To The End · "The beginning is the ending" Studio Guide Developer More Projects Built by Prashant Pandey · Inspired by Loki / Marvel Studios

title: FlowWrite — a writing application by Prashant Pandey
description: FlowWrite is Prashant Pandey’s writing application experiment, exploring rich documents, AI-assisted writing, history, and export.
content: FlowWrite A writing application I’m building to explore what a focused, flexible writing environment can be. FlowWrite brings together a quiet writing canvas, rich document formatting, AI-assisted writing features, document history, search, and export workflows. Its editor uses a transparent text input with a rendered layer for formatted content. Documents can include code, tables, images, and other structured material. I started FlowWrite because I wanted more control over how I write, organize, format, and export documents. Building it has given me practical questions to work through in interface design, document models, saving, import and export, and application architecture. What I’m exploring A calm writing interface with keyboard-first editing Rich document content and code blocks Local drafts, saving, and version history AI-assisted correction and continuation HTML and PDF export, with an optional native format FlowWrite is a work in progress. This page describes the project as it currently stands; details may change as I build and learn. Read the complete FlowWrite platform guide

title: FlowWrite Platform: Complete Guide
description: A detailed guide to the FlowWrite writing canvas, AI workflows, rich content, saving, search, import, and export systems.
content:
FlowWrite Platform Complete Guide & Showcase · All Features · All Workflows · All Systems Welcome to FlowWrite — the most intelligent, most elegant writing environment ever built for people who take their words seriously. This is not a word processor. This is a creative operating system: a pure writing canvas fused with a real-time AI partner, an intelligent save system, a powerful export engine, and a document library — all wrapped in a dark, luxurious interface. This guide covers every feature, every workflow, every system in FlowWrite. It is divided into four parts — paste them one after the other inside FlowWrite to experience every feature as you read about it. Part 1 · Editor & Workspace Part 2 · AI Systems Part 3 · Rich Content Part 4 · Export & Workflows Part 1 of 4 The Editor, The Workspace & The Universe The Editor Canvas — How It Actually Works The FlowWrite editor looks deceptively simple. A dark screen. A blinking cursor. EB Garamond serif font at 24 pixels with generous 1.625 line-spacing — the same typeface used by serious book publishers for three centuries. And nothing else visible. But underneath that simplicity is a remarkable engineering achievement: a four-layer rendering system that gives you the typing speed of a plain textarea and the visual richness of a full document editor simultaneously. architecture ⌘ Copy ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ BROWSER WINDOW │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ LAYER 4 — AI SYSTEM (silent) │ │ │ │ 3s debounce → paragraph detection → API call │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ LAYER 3 │ │ LAYER 1 — TRANSPARENT TEXTAREA │ │ │ │ GUTTER │ │ (handles all keyboard input & cursor) │ │ │ │ Numbers │ ├────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ ▸ Fold │ │ LAYER 2 — RICH RENDERING OVERLAY │ │ │ │ buttons │ │ (bold, italic, color, code blocks) │ │ │ └───────────┘ └────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ FOOTER STATS BAR (fades in/out) │ │ │ │ Title · Saved · 4m · 812w · 23p · 187L · 4391C │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Layer 1 — The Transparent Textarea: A native HTML textarea, visually invisible, at the very top of the stack. Every keystroke lands here. Zero lag between your fingers and the screen. Layer 2 — The Rich Rendering Overlay: A mirrored div behind the textarea, re-rendering your document in real time with bold, italic, colors, highlights, and code block rendering. Layer 3 — The Gutter System: Line Numbers gutter (sequential, toggleable) and Code Fold gutter (▸/▾ buttons to collapse/expand any code block). Layer 4 — The Silent AI Watcher: Every 3 seconds after you pause typing, the AI checks your current paragraph. If Auto-fix is enabled, it silently improves it. A tiny amber dot pulses → turns green → disappears. Your Complete Keyboard Shortcut Reference Shortcut Action Category Ctrl + K Open / Close the Panel drawer Navigation Ctrl + S Force-save to server immediately Save Ctrl + Z Undo — up to 150 steps back History Ctrl + Shift + Z Redo the undone action History Ctrl + B Bold the selected text Formatting Ctrl + I Italic the selected text Formatting Ctrl + U Underline the selected text Formatting Tab Request AI ghost-text autocomplete for current line AI Tab (again) Accept ghost-text and insert it into document AI Escape Dismiss ghost text / Close panel / End search mode General The Panel — Your Mission Control Center Press Ctrl+K anywhere. A panel glides in from the left with a spring animation. This is your hub for everything outside the writing canvas. ① AI Model Selector Switch Gemini / Groq / ChatGPT live. Status dot shows ChatGPT bridge health: green (ready), yellow (bridge running but not logged in), grey (bridge offline). ② Quick Actions Create new doc with today's date as title. Live search bar across all documents — 300ms debounce. Results show snippet + line number. ③ Recent Docs Last 3 modified documents. Hover to reveal inline rename. Click to switch instantly, cursor position preserved. ④ Library All documents with word counts. Rename, delete, upload .prash/.html/.txt files. Deduplicated titles auto-numbered. ⑤ AI Assistant Grammar fix (full doc), Rewrite with instruction, Auto-fix toggle, Line Numbers toggle — all AI controls in one place. ⑥ Version History Up to 100 snapshots per document. Triggered every 30s or on 5-word change. One-click restore — saves current state first. ⑦ Workspace Stats Total words, total documents, total AI fixes applied — your complete writing lifetime in 3 numbers. ⑧ Export Suite Preview (purple), .prash (gold), .html (green), .pdf (blue) — four export formats from the panel footer. Formatting — Bold, Italic, Color & Highlight Select any text — right-click for the context menu, or use keyboard shortcuts. Formatting is applied as invisible spans over the plain text, preserved through all export formats. This sentence shows bold text right next to italic text and underlined text all together. Color examples: Gold , Emerald , Sky Blue , Rose , Purple . Highlights: Sunburst Mint Lavender Sky Rose . And a strikethrough example for completeness. The Footer Stats Bar — Your Live Writing Vitals Move your mouse: the footer bar fades in. Stop for 2 seconds: it fades to 20% opacity. Every number updates on every single keystroke — no polling, no delay, pure live computation. The Great Gatsby — My Rewrite ✓ Saved READ 6m W 1,204 P 38 L 247 C 6,891 READ = words ÷ 200, rounded up. Code block content excluded. W = prose word count only (code tags stripped). P = paragraph count (blocks separated by 2+ newlines). L = visual line count (entire code blocks = exactly 1 line). C = character count excluding whitespace. The Save System — 4 Layers of Protection save timeline ⌘ Copy T+0ms You type: "The quick brown fox" T+1ms localStorage: draft saved instantly (browser storage) T+700ms Debounce timer fires — auto-save triggered T+701ms PATCH /api/documents/42 sent to server T+850ms Server: SQLite database updated T+851ms Server: data/backups/doc_42.json written (JSON backup) T+852ms Server: data/backups/markdown/My_Doc_42.md written T+860ms Footer: ✓ Saved (green check appears) T+860ms localStorage draft deleted (server save confirmed) // Layer 1: localStorage (instant, every keystroke) // Layer 2: 700ms debounce server auto-save // Layer 3: Ctrl+S manual immediate save // Layer 4: navigator.sendBeacon() on tab close (beforeunload) // If DB is lost: server startup runs syncAndRestoreDiskBackups() // Reads all JSON backups → re-inserts missing documents // ZERO DATA LOSS — disk always mirrors the database Version History — Time Travel for Your Writing Snapshots are taken automatically when 30 seconds pass since the last snapshot OR the word count changes by 5+ . Up to 100 snapshots per document. Before restoring any version, FlowWrite saves your current state first — so you can always go forward again. Full bidirectional time travel across sessions. Search Across All Your Writing search flow ⌘ Copy User types: "consciousness" Step 1: 300ms debounce fires Step 2: GET /api/search?q=consciousness Step 3: SQL LIKE query across title AND content of ALL documents Step 4: Returns up to 10 results with: - documentTitle, matchIndex, lineNumber - matchCount (total occurrences in doc) - snippet (120 chars around the match) - relevance (1.0 title match, 0.7 content match) Step 5: User clicks a result → Switch to that document Scroll to exact character position of match Highlight the matching text SearchNavHeader shows "1 of 14 matches" ← → arrows jump between all occurrences Escape closes the search navigation bar Continuing to Part 2 → AI Systems & All Workflows Part 2 of 4 AI Systems, Models & Complete AI Workflows Three AI Engines — Gemini, Groq, ChatGPT Property ✦ Gemini ⚡ Groq 🤖 ChatGPT Provider Google Groq Cloud OpenAI (Browser Automation) Model gemini-2.5-flash llama-3.3-70b-versatile ChatGPT Web (latest) Speed ~180 tok/s · Fast ~450 tok/s · Ultra-fast ~30 tok/s · Slow Parallelism 4 chunks at once 4 chunks at once 1 chunk at a time (serial) Fallback Chain 2.5 → 2.0 → 1.5-flash → 1.5-pro 3 retries, same model Requires main.py bridge API Key GEMINI_API_KEY GROQ_API_KEY No key — uses browser session Best For Default — reliable quality Speed-critical large docs No API key needed, free The Smart Chunking System FlowWrite's chunking pipeline splits long documents at paragraph boundaries, processes in parallel, then reassembles with perfect structural fidelity — zero blank-line changes, zero sentence splits. chunking pipeline ⌘ Copy Original document: 1,200 words · Max chunk size: 450 words STEP 1: Split at paragraph boundaries (2+ newlines) Store exact separator strings for lossless reassembly STEP 2: Group paragraphs into chunks ≤ 450 words each Never split mid-paragraph (would break sentence context) Result: 3 chunks of 440, 447, 313 words STEP 3: Build overlap tails — last 30 words of each chunk Passed as context to the next chunk's AI prompt Prevents continuity breaks at chunk boundaries STEP 4: Process in parallel (Gemini/Groq: 4 at a time) [Chunk 1 + Chunk 2] → sent simultaneously → ~800ms [Chunk 3] → sent after → ~400ms If a chunk fails: original text used as fallback STEP 5: Reassemble with exact original separators chunk1_result + sep1 + chunk2_result + sep2 + chunk3_result Total time for 1,200 words: ~1.2 seconds The AI Output Sanitizer — 5-Stage Cleaning sanitizer stages ⌘ Copy // RAW AI OUTPUT (before sanitizer): "Here is the corrected version of your text: The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog." // STAGE 1: Strip ChatGPT ... markers // STAGE 2: Strip XML wrapper tags (, , etc.) // STAGE 3: Strip markdown code fences (``` ... ```) // STAGE 4: Strip conversational preambles // "Here is the corrected version:" → REMOVED // "Sure! Here's the improved text:" → REMOVED // "Certainly, here is the revised passage:" → REMOVED // STAGE 5: Strip outer wrapping quotes ("..." or '...') // CLEAN OUTPUT (after sanitizer): The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog. AI Workflow 1 — Auto-Fix on Pause (3 Seconds) auto-fix logic ⌘ Copy onContentChange() → debounce(3000ms) → runDeltaFix() runDeltaFix(): if (!autoCorrect) return // Auto-fix disabled if (normCurrent === normLast) return // No meaningful change if (charDelta < 5) return // Change too tiny paragraph = getParagraphAtCursor() // Only the current para result = await POST("/api/ai/grammar-fix", { text: paragraph }) if (content !== contentAtCallStart) return // User typed → discard fixed = content.slice(0, para.start) + result.corrected + content.slice(para.end) setContent(fixed) // Silent update — cursor preserved // EXAMPLE: // You write: "She walkd into the room and it were quiet." // 3 seconds pass... // AI receives just that paragraph // AI returns: "She walked into the room and it was quiet." // Document silently updated. Amber dot → Green dot → Gone. AI Workflow 2 — Tab Autocomplete (Ghost Text) Press Tab at the end of any line. The AI receives your current line plus the last 800 characters of your document as context. It generates a 1–2 sentence natural continuation matching your exact tone, tense, and vocabulary. The suggestion appears as dim grey text immediately after your cursor. Press Tab again to accept. Type any character to dismiss. Press Escape to clear. autocomplete prompt ⌘ Copy // AUTOCOMPLETE PROMPT (actual prompt used in FlowWrite) Task: Write a natural 1-2 sentence continuation. Background context (style reference): [Last 600 characters of document for tone/topic context] Rules: 1. Continue DIRECTLY from the last word — no gap 2. Match tone, tense, vocabulary, writing style seamlessly 3. Do NOT repeat any text from the current writing 4. Return ONLY the continuation text — no wrappers Current writing: "The algorithm processes each node in the tree by visiting its left subtree first," // AI returns: " then the root node, and finally the right subtree — following the standard in-order traversal pattern." AI Workflow 3 — Selection Fix / Rewrite / Format Select any text → the Selection Action Bar appears at the bottom of the screen: selection ai modes ⌘ Copy MODE A — FIX Sends selection to grammar pipeline Rules: fix errors, preserve every word's meaning Before: "She don't know what happen. Everyone confuse." After: "She doesn't know what happened. Everyone was confused." MODE B — REWRITE (prompts for instruction) Instruction examples that work: · "make it more concise" → tightens sentences · "formal academic tone" → elevates vocabulary · "simplify for a 12-year-old" → removes jargon · "more dramatic and emotional"→ heightens tension · "convert to bullet points" → restructures as list Before: "The implementation of the aforementioned algorithmic solution necessitates comprehensive understanding..." Instruction: "make it simple and direct" After: "To implement this algorithm, you need to understand how it works." MODE C — FORMAT Structural cleanup ONLY — zero word changes Fixes: irregular spacing, inconsistent indentation, excessive blank lines, mis-aligned lists Temperature: 0.0 (completely deterministic) AI Activity Badge — What the Colors Mean AI Syncing (amber, pulsing) → AI Fixed (green, steady) → (disappears after 1.5s) The badge is position: fixed, top-right, pointer-events: none — it literally cannot be clicked. It never blocks your writing flow. Math & Technical Writing — AI Handles Everything FlowWrite is built for technical documents. title: About Prashant Pandey
description: Meet Prashant Pandey, a Grade 11 student who develops projects with AI coding tools and his own ideas.
content: About Prashant Pandey I’m Prashant Pandey, a Grade 11 student from Janakpur, Dhanusha, Nepal . I’m curious about how technology works, how ideas can become real projects, and what I can learn by trying to make something myself. I’m not a software professional, engineering-college student, or graduate. I’m a school student learning independently. For roughly three years, I’ve been exploring programming and making projects with help from AI coding tools, often through an iterative style people call vibe coding . I want this profile to be clear about that: AI tools help me write and revise code; the ideas, goals, product direction, and choices about what to explore come from me. How I learn and make things I learn by following questions. An idea leads me to research, try a tool, make a prototype, see what works, and decide what I want to understand next. I have experimented with many projects over the past few years. Some are small, some unfinished, and some have grown into longer projects. I share the process because the experiments and lessons are part of the work, too. Using AI coding tools has let me explore projects that might otherwise feel out of reach as a school student working on my own. It also gives me plenty to learn: how to describe a problem, assess generated code, make design decisions, notice limitations, and keep iterating toward something useful. I’m still developing my technical skills, and I try to be open about what I know and what I’m learning. FlowWrite FlowWrite is one of my main personal projects: a writing application shaped around my own ideas about how a flexible writing space could work. I’ve used Python, Node.js, and AI coding tools while developing it. The project explores rich documents, formatting, images, links, tables, code, saving, search, and exporting work to HTML or PDF. Making FlowWrite has given me a way to explore how an application fits together—from the writing canvas and document structure to saving, importing, and exporting. I’m continuing to improve it and learn from the decisions, prototypes, and problems along the way. You can [explore FlowWrite](/projects/flowwrite/) or read the [FlowWrite platform guide](/writing/flowwrite-platform-guide/). What I’m curious about My interests keep changing, but I often return to questions about how systems work. I’m exploring programming, web projects, artificial intelligence, computer vision, local and efficient AI, operating systems, computer architecture, C, assembly, and how computers start and run software. I’m also interested in mathematics, physics, filmmaking, and creative technology. I’m learning these subjects; I don’t claim to be an expert in them. I enjoy moving between a practical project and a bigger question, and I’m happy to label an idea as speculation when I haven’t established that it’s true. Ideas, writing, and learning in public Not every thought needs to become a product or a polished technical article. This website also gives me room for free writing: observations, questions, personal reflections, ideas, experiments, and topics I’m still working through. Sometimes writing helps me explain what I tried. Sometimes it helps me figure out what I think. I want the site to show a real learning journey rather than present a finished expert identity. Projects may change, experiments may fail, and my interests may lead somewhere I can’t predict yet. I’ll update the site as I learn and make more things. What I hope to do next I want to become more capable at understanding unfamiliar problems and turning my ideas into useful projects. I’m interested in learning more about computer science and AI, getting closer to the systems underneath everyday software, strengthening my foundations in mathematics and science, and exploring creative work beyond the screen. I haven’t chosen one fixed career path, and I’m still at school; these are directions I hope to explore over time. I welcome thoughtful feedback, mentorship, student-friendly opportunities, and collaborations that give me a chance to learn and contribute. If something I’ve made interests you, or you have a project, question, or opportunity you think I should see, [get in touch](/contact/). I don’t just want to know that something works. I want to understand why—and when I can’t find what I want to learn, I like trying to make it.

title: Contact Prashant Pandey
description: Get in touch with Prashant Pandey about projects, ideas, collaboration, feedback, or a conversation.
content: Questions about a project, an interesting idea, a correction, or a possible collaboration are all welcome. Email is the quickest way to reach me. You can also find me on the social and developer profiles below. I’m a student and don’t have a fixed response schedule, but I do my best to read genuine messages when I get the chance. You don’t need to be an expert or have a fully formed project to get in touch. What can we talk about? - A project, a bug, or a suggestion for something I’ve built - A technical question or something you’re trying to learn - A project, open-source, or learning collaboration - An idea, theory, experiment, or interesting problem - A correction, accessibility issue, or broken link on the website - Anything else you’d like to say A small privacy note The message form opens a draft in your email app; this website does not receive or store your message. Please don’t include passwords, private credentials, financial information, or other sensitive details.
